# Cittaṭṭhitikathā (Kv 2.7)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cittaṭṭhitikathā* ("Controversy on the Duration of Consciousness") is a debate within the *Kathāvatthu* of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The controversy addresses the persistence of mind, disputing the view that certain mental states endure for a prolonged period [von Rospatt 1995]. According to the *Kathāvatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the refuted proposition that consciousness or mental entities can abide for a long time was maintained by the Andhakas [von Rospatt 1995]. In his analysis of the development of the Buddhist theory of momentariness, Alexander von Rospatt highlights the *Cittaṭṭhitikathā* as representing an early phase of debate focusing on the transitoriness of mental events—contrasting with the bodily aggregate, in dialogue with canonical discourses like the *Assutavāsutta* (SN 12.61)—well before the universal momentariness of all conditioned phenomena was formulated in later sections of the work such as the *Khaṇikakathā* [von Rospatt 1995].
